lines.trans: Rodion Sergeyevich, where did you learn to cook so wonderfully?
I do not remember, Viktor Petrovich, I remember nothing at all.
My head forgot, but my hands remember everything well.
We must definitely celebrate this, come with me quickly!
Hi, Vika! How are things? I missed you a lot.
I have an important meeting with a girl tonight.
With a very beautiful girl named Vika.
Allow me to introduce: the star and face of our restaurant, Dmitry!

words.gloss: to imagine, to picture; to introduce

lines.trans: Very nice to meet you, and in person you are even younger, Kristina.
All Kristinas are the most faithful and kind wives.
Maybe I should not drink? I have not eaten properly today.
You will have a snack at the same time! Rodion Sergeyevich, to you!

examples.trans: Allow me to introduce myself, my name is Rodion Sergeyevich.

examples.text: Позвольте представить: звезда и лицо нашего ресторана Дмитрий!
examples.trans: Allow me to introduce: the star and face of our restaurant, Dmitry!

examples.text: Виктор Петрович, можете себе представить, это моя жена!
examples.trans: Viktor Petrovich, can you imagine, this is my wife!

meanings.en: star (in the sky, hotel rating, or famous person)
meanings.note: Common feminine noun meaning 'star' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Позвольте представить: звезда и лицо нашего ресторана Дмитрий!
examples.trans: Allow me to introduce: the star and face of our restaurant, Dmitry!

examples.text: Не пять звёзд, конечно.
examples.trans: Not five stars, of course.

examples.text: На небе горят яркие звёзды.
examples.trans: Bright stars shine in the sky.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian clause-linking conjunction meaning 'and', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Мне кажется, здесь будет очень тихо и уютно.
examples.trans: It seems to me it will be very quiet and cozy here.

examples.text: Во дворе нет ни машин, ни прохожих.
examples.trans: In the courtyard there are neither cars nor passersby.

examples.text: А ещё можно поставить тут газовый обогреватель.
examples.trans: And we can also put a gas heater out here.

meanings.note: Common neuter noun meaning 'face' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Об этом вы завтра поговорите с полицией.
examples.trans: You will talk about that with the police tomorrow.

examples.text: Мне в полицию попадать совсем не хотелось бы.
examples.trans: I would not like to end up at the police station at all.

examples.text: А твоё дело по контракту — здесь лицом торговать.
examples.trans: And your job by contract is to be the face here.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'our', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Думаю, что скоро буду в нашем ресторане.
examples.trans: I think that I will be at our restaurant soon.

examples.text: Попроси его, чтобы он нашего бомжа не трогал.
examples.trans: Ask him not to touch our homeless man.

examples.text: Мне сказали, что ты выгоняешь нашего ресторанного бомжа.
examples.trans: I was told that you are kicking out our restaurant homeless man.

meanings.note: Borrowed from French 'restaurant' (from 'restaurer', to restore strength with rich broth); entered Russian in the early 19th century.

examples.text: Думаю, что скоро буду в нашем ресторане.
examples.trans: I think that I will be at our restaurant soon.

examples.text: Меня в этом ресторане услышат!
examples.trans: They will hear me in this restaurant!

examples.text: Мне сказали, что ты выгоняешь нашего ресторанного бомжа.
examples.trans: I was told that you are kicking out our restaurant homeless man.

meanings.note: Prefix 'при-' indicates approaching, attachment, or slight degree of action (stem 'ятный'). Adjective formed with the common Slavic suffix '-н-' from a noun/verb root. Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('pleasant').

examples.text: Приятного мне аппетита! Витя, чего ты хотел?
examples.trans: Bon appétit to me! Vitya, what did you want?

examples.text: Очень приятно, а в жизни вы ещё моложе, Кристина.
examples.trans: Very nice to meet you, and in person you are even younger, Kristina.

examples.text: Я её ещё не вспомнил, но от этого ещё приятнее.
examples.trans: I have not remembered her yet, but that makes it even nicer.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian spatial or relational preposition meaning 'in, into', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Вот здесь можно сделать вторую летнюю веранду.
examples.trans: Right here we can build a second summer veranda.

examples.text: Во дворе нет ни машин, ни прохожих.
examples.trans: In the courtyard there are neither cars nor passersby.

examples.text: А ещё можно поставить тут газовый обогреватель.
examples.trans: And we can also put a gas heater out here.

meanings.note: Common feminine noun meaning 'life' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Видимо, время в моей жизни летит очень быстро.
examples.trans: Apparently, time in my life flies very fast.

examples.text: Очень приятно, а в жизни вы ещё моложе, Кристина.
examples.trans: Very nice to meet you, and in person you are even younger, Kristina.

examples.text: Такая жизнь.
examples.trans: That's life.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian conversational adverb meaning 'else/more', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: А ещё можно поставить тут газовый обогреватель.
examples.trans: And we can also put a gas heater out here.

examples.text: Подождите, это ещё что такое во дворе?
examples.trans: Wait a minute, what on earth is that in the courtyard?

examples.text: Да, привет, Вика! Нет, я ещё не на работе.
examples.trans: Yes, hi, Vika! No, I am not at work yet.

meanings.note: Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('younger').

examples.text: Молодой человек, как на тест-драйв записаться?
examples.trans: Young man, how do I sign up for a test drive?

examples.text: У них молодая семья.
examples.trans: They have a young family.

examples.text: Молодой человек, а как на тест-драйв записаться?
examples.trans: Young man, how do I sign up for a test drive?

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'all', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Завтра здесь будут ужинать важные инвесторы с женой.
examples.trans: Tomorrow important investors and a wife will have dinner here.

examples.text: Посмотри, какой ты дерзкий! Может, тебя отсюда вывести?
examples.trans: Look how cheeky you are! Maybe I should escort you out of here?

examples.text: Всё нормально.
examples.trans: Everything's fine.

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'амый'). Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('the most').

examples.text: Я имею право набирать поваров сам по своему контракту.
examples.trans: I have the right to hire cooks myself under my contract.

examples.text: Сегодня вечером в зале наши самые главные гости.
examples.trans: Tonight our most important guests are in the dining room.

examples.text: Я легко могу и сам дома всё приготовить.
examples.trans: I can easily cook everything myself at home.

meanings.note: Adjective formed with the common Slavic suffix '-н-' from a noun/verb root. Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('faithful / loyal').

examples.text: Вернее было бы сказать: это кто такой?
examples.trans: It would be more accurate to say: who is this?

examples.text: Все Кристины — это самые верные и добрые жёны.
examples.trans: All Kristinas are the most faithful and kind wives.

examples.text: Извините, я, наверное, уже тихо пойду домой.
examples.trans: Excuse me, I should probably quietly go home now.

meanings.note: Prefix 'до-' marks reaching a boundary or finishing the remainder of an action (stem 'брый'). Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('kind').

examples.text: Добрый день, позвольте нарушить вашу тихую беседу.
examples.trans: Good afternoon, allow me to interrupt your quiet conversation.

examples.text: Понимаешь, в Москве существуют такие добрые традиции.
examples.trans: You see, in Moscow there are such kind traditions.

examples.text: Доброе утро, шеф! Как ваше настроение сегодня?
examples.trans: Good morning, Chef! How is your mood today?

meanings.note: Common feminine noun meaning 'wife' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Как это замуж? Я не собираюсь на ней жениться!
examples.trans: What do you mean married? I am not going to marry her!

examples.text: Завтра здесь будут ужинать важные инвесторы с женой.
examples.trans: Tomorrow important investors and a wife will have dinner here.

examples.text: Жена твоя большая поклонница, посидишь с ними, пошутишь.
examples.trans: The wife is a big fan of yours, you will sit and joke with them.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian conversational adverb meaning 'maybe', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Вот здесь можно сделать вторую летнюю веранду.
examples.trans: Right here we can build a second summer veranda.

examples.text: А ещё можно поставить тут газовый обогреватель.
examples.trans: And we can also put a gas heater out here.

examples.text: А может быть, лучше выпьем за нашу любовь?
examples.trans: Or maybe it is better to drink to our love?

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'тоять'). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'is standing', paired with 'постоять'.

examples.text: Его паспорт и настоящую медицинскую книжку повара.
examples.trans: His passport and a real cook's medical booklet.

examples.text: Макс, успокойся, у тебя уже настоящая паранойя!
examples.trans: Max, calm down, you already have real paranoia!

examples.text: Такие настоящие документы даже у меня есть не все.
examples.trans: Even I do not have all such authentic documents.

meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'drink', paired with 'выпить'.

related.gloss: to go on a drinking binge

examples.text: Может, не стоит пить? Я сегодня толком не ел.
examples.trans: Maybe I should not drink? I have not eaten properly today.

examples.text: Я пью чай.
examples.trans: I'm drinking tea.

examples.text: Он не пьёт.
examples.trans: He doesn't drink.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian conversational adverb meaning 'properly', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Может, не стоит пить? Я сегодня толком не ел.
examples.trans: Maybe I should not drink? I have not eaten properly today.

examples.text: Макс сказал это совершенно толком и спокойно.
examples.trans: Max said this quite properly and calmly.

meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'ate', paired with 'съесть'.

examples.text: Да, это факт, место здесь очень уютное.
examples.trans: Yes, that is a fact, the place here is very cozy.

examples.text: Думаю, что скоро буду в нашем ресторане.
examples.trans: I think that I will be at our restaurant soon.

examples.text: Да, Вика, я тебе честно это обещаю.
examples.trans: Yes, Vika, I honestly promise you that.

заодно.gloss: at the same time, while I'm at it

meanings.en: at the same time, while one is at it
meanings.note: Prefix 'за-' marks beginning an action, covering, or stopping by along the way (stem 'одно'). Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.text: Заодно и перекусите! Родион Сергеевич, пью за вас!
examples.trans: You will have a snack at the same time! Rodion Sergeyevich, to you!

examples.text: Заодно ветки во дворе постригу.
examples.trans: And at the same time I'll trim the branches in the yard.

examples.text: Купи хлеб и заодно молоко.
examples.trans: Buy bread and milk while you're at it.

meanings.en: to have a quick bite to eat, to snack
meanings.note: Prefix 'пере-' denotes crossing over, repeating, or exceeding a limit (stem 'кусить'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'you will have a snack', paired with 'перекусывать'.

related.gloss: to have a bite to eat

examples.text: У вас не будет перекусить? Со вчерашнего дня ни крошки.
examples.trans: Would you have a bite to eat? Not a crumb since yesterday.

examples.text: Заодно и перекусите! Родион Сергеевич, пью за вас!
examples.trans: You will have a snack at the same time! Rodion Sergeyevich, to you!

examples.text: Проходи, присядь, перекуси.
examples.trans: Come in, sit down, have a bite to eat.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian spatial or relational preposition meaning 'for', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Вернее было бы сказать: это кто такой?
examples.trans: It would be more accurate to say: who is this?

examples.text: Я любитель остатков пищи этого чудного заведения.
examples.trans: I am a connoisseur of leftovers from this wonderful establishment.

examples.text: И сколько московских бомжей кормится за мой счёт?
examples.trans: And how many Moscow homeless people eat at my expense?
